surprises.description: Corning guided Q4 sales to $5.2–$5.3 billion and EPS to $0.96–$1.00, above the preview’s $5.02 billion and $0.88 consensus estimates. The EPS range also exceeds the preview’s base-case Q4 range of $0.92–$0.95.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 guidance calls for ~19% sales growth to $5.2-5.3 billion and ~36% EPS growth to $0.96-$1.00.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 consensus is ~$5.02B / $0.88”; the Base scenario expected “$5.15–5.30B / $0.92–0.95.”

surprises.description: Q3 sales of $5.1 billion and EPS of $0.91 both exceeded the preview’s $5.02 billion and $0.88 consensus. The sales beat was modest, while the EPS beat was somewhat larger.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 sales grew 19% year-over-year to $5.1 billion and EPS rose 36% to $0.91, both exceeding guidance.”

surprises.description: Optical Communications substantially outperformed the preview’s growth and profit estimates: sales were $2.4 billion rather than $2.23 billion, and net income was $532 million rather than $479 million. Enterprise sales rose 84% and Gen AI product sales more than doubled, indicating stronger demand in the growth areas the preview was watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Optical Communications sales grew 44% year-over-year to $2.4 billion with net income up 80% to $532 million, driven by Enterprise sales up 84% and Gen AI product sales up over 100%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Optical Communications | $2.23B | +34.9% | $479M”; the preview asked “how much of Enterprise growth is Gen-AI product (higher margin) vs. commodity fiber.”

surprises.description: Margins beat the preview’s approximate expectations, especially operating margin: gross margin was 40.5% versus about 40%, and operating margin was 22.7% versus about 21%. Corning expanded both despite the capacity ramp risks highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Corning expanded gross margin 150 bps to 40.5%, operating margin 310 bps to 22.7%, and ROIC 330 bps to 16.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Core gross margin ~40%” and “Core operating margin ~21%,” and flagged start-up costs, helium, and energy costs as risks to margins.

surprises.description: New long-term agreements with Zayo, Verizon, and AT&T led management to say the DCI opportunity will exceed its prior $1 billion target in both size and timing. That is stronger and earlier than the preview’s view that the Verizon and AT&T agreements would mostly contribute revenue in 2027 and that Carrier could remain soft.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New long-term agreements with Zayo, Verizon and AT&T support management's view that the DCI opportunity will exceed the previously communicated $1 billion target in both size and timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Verizon and AT&T agreements were “mostly 2027 revenue, so Carrier may stay soft.”

surprises.description: Management reiterated that optical scale-up will accelerate in 2028 and described potential fiber demand per GPU rising tenfold. This gives a firmer, more bullish timing signal than the preview’s warning that optical technology penetration timing was hard to predict.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reiterated conviction that optical scale-up will accelerate in 2028, which could drive a potential 10-fold increase in fiber demand per GPU (from 16 to 160 fibers).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that management had flagged “the timing of new optical technology penetration” as “hard to predict.”

surprises.description: Glass Innovations declined, with sales down 3% and net income down 10%; notebooks and handhelds were down about 20%. That points to weaker markets than the preview’s already-negative mid-teens full-year handheld outlook, although the price increase aimed at 2027 could help later.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Glass Innovations sales fell 3% to $1.5 billion with net income down 10% to $328 million amid weak markets (notebooks/handhelds down ~20%), prompting a display glass price increase geared toward 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Handheld units [were] guided down mid-teens for the full year on memory-price-driven device pricing.”

surprises.description: Solar remained loss-making at a $7 million net loss, rather than improving toward the breakeven result the preview identified as a possible Q3 tailwind. The reported pricing improvement and longer-term growth opportunity are favorable, but did not change the current-quarter loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Solar sales rose 37% year-over-year to $436 million but posted a $7 million net loss, with Section 232 trade action improving pricing as Corning builds toward a $3 billion-plus revenue stream with above-average profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Solar had a “$7M loss in Q2” and management was “guiding to improvement in Q3”; it described “a Solar breakeven” as a potential EPS tailwind.

surprises.description: Customer deposits and free cash flow provided a source of funding for growth spending that the preview had not highlighted: deposits funded the majority of growth-related capital spending. This offers some offset to the preview’s concern about the ATM and potential dilution, though the facts do not say whether the ATM was used.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer deposits contributed $639 million to operating cash flow in the first nine months, funding the majority of growth-related capital spending as part of the ~$2 billion 2026 CapEx plan”; Corning generated “$661 million in free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the “$2B at-the-market equity authorization” an “open wound” and asked how much had been drawn.
